name: PROTEIN - S ANTIGEN (FREE)
interpretation:
Protein S is a vitamin K-dependent glycoprotein present in platelets and synthesized within the liver and endothelial cells.
• Physiologically, protein S has an essential anticoagulant function. It possesses both APC-dependent and independent anticoagulant properties and thus is an important guardian in controlling thrombin generation and fibrinolysis.
• Out of the total plasma protein S, approximately 60% circulates in a bound form with the C4b binding protein (C4bBP) while the remaining 40% circulates as "free" protein S. Only free protein S has anticoagulant function.
• Protein S deficiency may be associated with 3 to 10 fold increased risk of venous thrombosis, recurrent miscarriage, complications of pregnancy (preeclampsia, abruptio placentae, intrauterine growth restriction, and stillbirth) and possibly arterial thrombosis.
• Congenital Protein S deficiency- is rare autosomal dominant disorder with 1 to 3% incidence of venous thromboembolism in adults.
• Acquired deficiencies of protein C may occur in association with vitamin K deficiency, oral anticoagulation with coumarin compound,liver disease and DIC.
Comments : Patients on oral anticoagulants will have decreased protein S antigen level. Patients should be off oral anticoagulant therapy for two weeks for accurate measurement of protein S antigen levels. Free protein S levels decreases during pregnancy.
